summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for management following a procedure to address recurrent airway stenosis. He underwent microlaryngoscopy with balloon dilation and bronchial dilation due to severe stenosis in the left mainstem bronchus and bronchus intermedius, complications of his underlying connective tissue disorder with polychondritis. Post-procedure, he was stabilized on supplemental humidified oxygen and started on a short-term prednisone taper (60 mg for two days, then step-down) and Bactrim for infection prophylaxis. His white blood cell count rose to 19.2, attributed to steroid use or procedural inflammation, with no signs of infection. He remained in no acute distress, with stable vital signs and a clear chest X-ray. He was discharged home with follow-up arranged in rheumatology, ENT, and pulmonology, and instructions to continue trach care with humidification and medication tapering.
